A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Policy World Model paper, with 20 readable pages including Appendices A–C. Text and rendered pages match apart from the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original PWM planning and video-generation results, benchmark comparisons, ablations and qualitative analyses in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original experimental results, including nuScenes and NAVSIM evaluations and the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The context-guided tokenizer, action-free forecasting, parallel frame-token generation, Dynamic Focal Loss and collaborative planning procedure are identical in Section 3 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same OpenDV-YouTube, nuScenes and NAVSIM coverage, auxiliary CC12M/FineWeb tasks and nuPlan frame sourcing. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in the nuScenes and NAVSIM comparisons (main Tables 1–2), including their separate input and ego-status settings.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain identical splits, preprocessing, input histories, prediction horizons, training budgets, evaluation metrics and testing procedures.

E4.justification: The pretraining, data-scale, forecasting-horizon, Dynamic Focal Loss and text-generation ablations are unchanged. The temporal-latent analysis and qualitative comparisons in Appendices B–C are also identical.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-estimate reporting. Neither reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative results match across the main text and appendices. For example, main Table 1 retains PWM average collision rates of 0.07% without ego status and 0.04% with it; Table 2 retains NAVSIM PDMS of 88.1.

T1.justification: The token definitions, probabilistic formulations and loss equations (1)–(4) are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about unified forecasting and planning, efficient generation and competitive performance using only front-camera input.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretations of forecasting, safety versus progress and limited benefits from text generation. The poor-visibility and short-planning-horizon limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and data-processing instructions in Section 4.1 and Appendix A are identical. Both retain the same promised code/model release and repository link.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works and all 74 references are unchanged, as is the positioning against separate and unified world-model/planning approaches.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1, 22 Oct 2025, to v2, 25 Nov 2025. The title, authors, prose, headings and document structure are identical.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions and page layout are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. Pages 2–20 render identically, and page 1 is identical outside the version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: The complete scientific content, experimental evidence, reproducibility information and presentation are unchanged. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp provides no meaningful improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
